name: Ohio

response.rule_text: Offices must promptly prepare records for inspection and provide copies within a reasonable period of time (R.C. 149.43(B)(1)); no fixed day count.

fees.labor_rule: Cost means actual cost of depleted supplies, not labor (Data Trace per RCFP); inspection cannot be conditioned on a fee.
fees.copy_rule: Copies at cost (§ 149.43(B)); advance payment for mailed copies limited to postage and supplies (§ 149.43(B)(6),(7)).
fees.late_penalty: Statutory damages $100 per business day up to $1,000 for hand/certified-mail requests (§ 149.43(C)); attorney fees discretionary.

residency.rule_text: Any person may request, not limited to citizens (§ 149.43(B)); incarcerated persons need a judge's consent unless records support a justiciable claim (§ 149.43(B)(8)).

appeal.body: Court of Claims (R.C. 2743.75) or mandamus in common pleas, court of appeals or Supreme Court
appeal.rule_text: No administrative appeal or AG role; aggrieved person files Court of Claims complaint ($25 fee, no deadline stated) or mandamus (R.C. 149.43(C)(1)), six years from accrual per RCFP (R.C. 2305.07); cannot do both for the same request.

exemptions_citation: Ohio Rev. Code § 149.43(A)(1) (exceptions for records prohibited by state or federal law)
format_rule: Electronic records: requester may choose paper, original medium, or another medium the office can reasonably duplicate (§ 149.43(B)(6)); no duty to create records.
notes: Read chars 0-100k and 190-290k. Governor: separation of powers may limit application to Governor and other statewide officials per Ohio Supreme Court (RCFP). Delay itself gives standing to sue (DiFranco 2014). Legislature: certain staff records excluded by R.C. 101.30. exemptions_citation partly inferred from RCFP text; full list not read.
